spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (CONNECTING: valid but state-forbidden Frame -> Error(402)+Close(402); 401/402 split by error nature)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.4 invariant 2 (subscription cannot complete before pairing/auth/negotiation)
description: CONNECTING receives a VALID Subscribe — well-formed and decodable, but state-forbidden: Error(402)+Close(402) (INVALID_STATE), never 401 MALFORMED_MESSAGE.
preconditions: Fresh connection: transport handshake done, control stream open, no app message processed yet — state CONNECTING.
Isolated connection; request_id counter starts at 1.
assertions: The Subscribe is VALID — it decodes cleanly with no validation failure — so the answer is 402 INVALID_STATE, never 401: the CONNECTING code follows the error's NATURE (malformed/generic-validation -> 401, valid-but-state-forbidden -> 402; spec §5.2).
The Error echoes the request's request_id (1) — proof the request was understood (a malformed frame could not echo one).
402 is fatal here (paired with Close): the session never leaves CONNECTING; the non-fatal, connection-kept 402 exists only for a duplicate Subscribe in READY/PLAYING (spec §5.2 error classes).
Message-specific CONNECTING rows keep precedence: a PairingRequest, capacity exhaustion, or a second Client stream follows its own row, not this generic one (spec §5.2).
Media subscription can never complete before pairing/auth/negotiation/configuration by state legality; violations produce a defined error, never a silent ignore (spec §5.4).
